cards.title: la = her / it (feminine word)
cards.body: Change lo's o to a and you get la: 'her', or 'it' for a feminine word. Gender belongs to the word, not the object; words ending in -a are usually feminine, like casa (house).

examples.en: I want to see it (the house).

cards.title: Formal or informal you?
cards.body: La can also be formal 'you' to a woman (lo to a man). How much formal speech is used varies a lot: in Spain people often start formally with strangers, while in Buenos Aires the formal form is rare. The safe default: start formal and adjust to how people speak to you.
cards.caveat: This varies by region and situation; there's no single rule.

cards.title: quiere = he / she / it wants, you (formal) want
cards.body: Just like es, these four meanings go together. The -e ending is the 'he/she/it/you formal' form.

cards.title: Questions: just use your voice
cards.body: Spanish doesn't need 'do'. Keep the same words and raise your voice like a question. In writing, questions open with ¿.

examples.en: Do you want to visit me?
Don't you want to visit me?

cards.title: por qué = why (and porque = because)
cards.body: The same sounds also mean 'because'. Written as two words with an accent for 'why' (por qué) and one word for 'because' (porque).

examples.en: Why don't you want to visit me?

cards.caveat: The spelling difference (por qué vs porque) is standard Spanish; the lesson only says they sound the same.

cards.title: venir = to come
cards.body: Usually said with a soft b. Link it to conveniente ('coming together') and bienvenido (welcome: bien = well + venido = come).

cards.title: la casa, a la casa
cards.body: La also means 'the' before a feminine word. Venir is a verb of movement, so it takes a before another verb.

examples.en: Do you want to come to the house?
Why don't you want to come to visit me?
examples.es: ¿Por qué no quiere venir a visitarme?

cards.title: debo = I owe → I must
cards.body: Debo means 'I owe' (the silent b in English 'debt' comes from it). Followed by a verb, it means 'I must'.

practice.en: Do you (formal) want to visit me?
Don't you (formal) want to visit me?
Why don't you (formal) want to visit me?
Do you (formal) want to come to the house?
Do you (formal) want to come to visit me?
practice.why: venir is movement: venir a visitarme.
